text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed console sampling and route attribution jumpy after last SDK init reorder in py/ts/go clients. Traces show sampling flag set after routemeta is emitted so console buckets are off.
liam: ugh. is this the change where init() became lazy? :thinking_face:
jess: yes, introduced lazy init to avoid cold-start cost. but it defers telemetry handshake until first request.
manual example:
`# in python client\nclient = RedwoodClient()  # lazy\nclient.generate(...)  # triggers init & telemetry` 
anita: so route metadata packets sometimes go out with default sampling 0.0 and later ones 1.0 -> console splits them across two charts.
maya: exact. dashboard shows two nearly-identical routes as separate lines, making quota alerts noisy.
liam: short term workaround — call client._ensure_init() or do an explicit client.init() on app startup.
jess: agreed. we should expose a public client.init() in all three libs (py/ts/go) rather than forcing people to call private APIs.
eng-platform: plan: patch runtime to send routemeta only after handshake completes OR buffer routemeta until init finishes. what's lower risk?
anita: buffering seems safer (no perf regression) — hold first routemeta per process and flush post-handshake.
maya: can we toggle buffering via env var so we can roll back quickly? :thumbsup:
eng-platform: yes — add REDWOOD_BUFFER_ROUTEMETA=true default false for canary. then flip for prod after 24h.
liam: i'll draft a tiny SDK PR for python + typescript that adds client.init() and optional env buffer. assign to @jess for review.
jess: thanks — will also add a console hint explaining the temporary split (notice) and link to workaround docs.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist: create feature flag, update console docs, add telemetry unit test, coordinate canary across regions.
manual follow-up: PR links once ready — https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/XXXX (placeholder).
